title: VXAce Do you know how to switch to second event & have a moment where a character will say "Hey, this is still an issue" in a loop and repeat the 1st event

posts.author: DeadManDan98
posts.body:
Hey, you know me for making a fan game but I need help to make a first event and after the first event is done, I will have a second event where the character will say that there's still a problem and have it looped on the second event.
But I am not too familiar with events, I mean, I did a few cutscenes on other game projects with a help of YouTube tutorials but not this one, is there a way to do this?

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
it depends on whether you want this to be a single cutscene or have the player manually go between events.
if it is a single automatic cutscene, you don't switch to the second event but remotely control that second event.
if it is supposed to be two different actions then you use switches to check the quest status and give different answers dependign on the switch.
in all cases I strongly suggest you follow the link to the starting point in my signature and work through the tutorials linked there to learn the basics for the engine.
and by that I really mean working through as in doing what they describe on their own, just reading (or watching) a tutorial is always a waste of your time if you don't spent the time in the editor to proof what you learned.

posts.author: gstv87
posts.body:
have a variable trigger the actual release of the event at value > X.
make that X as much as how many individual half-steps there are.
increase by 1 every time a half-step is done.
as long as the player doesn't complete all half-steps (getting X to threshold), the sequence should loop.
IDK what you want exactly... that's how I'd set it up: progress can only go forward.
but you can "forward" a collection of half-steps (each, binary) when putting them in sequence, since you can only go from one to the other, one at a time, in any random sequence.
(...unless, you want them sequenced, which is an extra check or two)
